messages:
anya: we need to reconsider our adapter manifest shape. current manifest tries to be 'one manifest to rule them all' and it's leaking mode-specific bits everywhere. feels brittle when adding new hosted-only capabilities.

matt: agree. can you sketch the main problems you're seeing?

anya: sure — three pain points: 1) secret surfaces differ (kms vs customer-kms vs no-kms) and we end up with a lot of optional fields + weird validation rules; 2) capability flags live in ad-hoc places so fallback routing must inspect deep fields; 3) telemetry hooks are duplicated across adapters. those make rollouts and tests messy.

reza: +1. also tests: we currently assert manifest JSON equality in a few places which breaks on tiny reconciler refactors. orthogonality would help.

olivia: idea: split manifest into a small core (contract) + mode extensions. core = identity, endpoints, minimal auth descriptor, capability references (names, not blobs). extensions live in namespaced keys that adapters opt into. that keeps validation and UI focused.

cheng: could look like: 
```
core: {
  id: "r-prod-1",
  adapter_version: "v2",
  capabilities: ["streaming","kv-cache"],
  auth: { type: "bearer", authority: "controlplane" }
}
extensions.hosted: { billing_plan: "metered", fast_fallback: true }
extensions.private: { vpc_subnets: [...], kms_profile: "customer" }
```
This keeps the core small.

anya: exactly this direction. a few followups: - how do we express capability compatibility (eg hosted provides streaming but private can only do non-streaming unless a specific runtime is present)? - how to signal fallbacks (route to cheaper model variant) without coupling to extension internals?

matt: capability compatibility could be a typed capability descriptor in core: 
`capabilities: [{name: "streaming", min_runtime: "rt-2", guaranteed: false}]` 
then the planner can decide if a runtime satisfies it. keep all runtime/implementation details in extension metadata.

reza: for fallbacks we should reference capability names + a policy id. e.g. `fallback_policy: { prefer: ["low_cost_variant"], policy_ref: "policy://canary-2" }` that keeps routing logic separate from secrets/config.

olivia: validation rules: core schema strict; extension schemas versioned and validated by owning teams. that avoids core churn. also propose a simple adapter discovery call that returns supported capabilities at runtime (fast probe) so planner doesn't need to deep-parse manifests for presence.

anya: sounds good. would like to preserve a small set of standard capability names (streaming, kv-cache, quantized, embeddings, tool-calls, rerank) so we don't drift. can infra own the registry?

infra-bot: NOTE: registry-service currently exists as `cap-registry` — can add REST endpoint for declarative list. will add backlog ticket if we get sign-off.

cheng: operational concerns: secret flows — core should only include a secret reference (eg `auth.secret_ref`) and extension declares what kind of secret it expects (kms vs token). realization of secret (KMS key id) stays out of the manifest except as opaque refs. that prevents accidental leakage in hosted manifests stored in control plane.

matt: agree, avoid embedding actual credentials. also, telemetry hooks: core exposes `telemetry_sink_refs` and extensions declare events they emit. console/UI can then map and aggregate.

anya: tradeoffs? might make simple hosted-only changes slightly more verbose because you must place things under `extensions.hosted`. but tradeoff worth it for clarity and fewer accidental regressions.

reza: rollout plan suggestion: 1) create core+extensions schema RFC, 2) implement adapter discovery probe + capability registry integration (read-only) for 2 weeks, 3) migrate one small adapter (eg a legacy dedicated adapter) behind a feature flag, 4) run shadow validation, 5) flip. keep conversion tooling in controlplane repo.

olivia: testing checklist: manifest converter tests, schema compatibility tests, planner unit tests (capability satisfaction), and e2e fallback scenarios.

anya: i'll draft the RFC with example JSON, validation matrix, and migration plan. will call out the minimal CLI `manifest-lint` that teams run locally to avoid breakage.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-4123 "cap-registry endpoint for manifest capability lookup" — assigned to infra-team backlog.

matt: thumbs up. small nit: ensure migration doesn't change public adapter APIs — keep adapter-facing payload stable for a transition window.

anya: noted. thanks everyone — i'll post draft RFC in #architecture-rfcs in 24h. :thumbsup:

olivia: :clap:

cheng: thanks, good direction.
